item.title: TT-104: Undo for TaskStore (add, complete, delete)
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The library is in the `tasktracker/` package and tests in `tests/`; the README and BACKLOG.md are at the repo root. Standard library only. Run the tests from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; they must all pass.

Implement exactly this ticket from BACKLOG.md (TT-104), and nothing from TT-101 to TT-103:

`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Add unit tests covering each acceptance point, including LIFO ordering across mixed kinds, restoring a deleted task exactly (fields and id), id non-reuse after undoing an add, and failed operations not being recorded. Keep the undo bookkeeping explicit (a simple stack of records), and avoid storing aliases of mutable task objects that could change later. Commit only this ticket's change, with a commit message that names TT-104, using the repository's configured git identity. Do not add any Co-Authored-By, "generated by" or tool-attribution lines to the commit message. Do not touch files for other tickets.

The spec asks for an exact restore under the same id, not the same object, so this is non-blocking.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax in tasktracker.search.search
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The library is in the `tasktracker/` package and tests in `tests/`; the README and BACKLOG.md are at the repo root. Standard library only. Run the tests from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; they must all pass.

Implement exactly this ticket from BACKLOG.md (TT-103), and nothing from TT-101, TT-102 or TT-104:

`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Add unit tests covering each acceptance point, including quoted phrases, unterminated quotes, unknown fields and statuses, and blank queries. Commit only this ticket's change, with a commit message that names TT-103, using the repository's configured git identity. Do not add any Co-Authored-By, "generated by" or tool-attribution lines to the commit message. Do not touch files for other tickets.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export in tasktracker.export.to_csv
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The library is in the `tasktracker/` package and tests in `tests/`; the README and BACKLOG.md are at the repo root. Standard library only. Run the tests from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; they must all pass.

Implement exactly this ticket from BACKLOG.md (TT-102), and nothing from TT-101 or TT-103/TT-104:

`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Add unit tests covering each acceptance point, including titles with commas, quotes, CR and LF, and empty tags/due. Prefer the standard `csv` module only if its output matches the rules exactly (quoting rules and CRLF line terminator); otherwise write the small explicit formatter. Commit only this ticket's change, with a commit message that names TT-102, using the repository's configured git identity. Do not add any Co-Authored-By, "generated by" or tool-attribution lines to the commit message. Do not touch files for other tickets.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in tasktracker.dates.parse_due
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The library is in the `tasktracker/` package and tests in `tests/`; the README and BACKLOG.md are at the repo root. Standard library only. Run the tests from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; they must all pass.

Implement exactly this ticket from BACKLOG.md (TT-101), and nothing from TT-102 to TT-104:

`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Add unit tests covering each acceptance point. Keep functions short and validate inputs at the boundary. Commit only this ticket's change, with a clear commit message that names TT-101, using the repository's configured git identity. Do not add any Co-Authored-By, "generated by" or tool-attribution lines to the commit message. Do not touch files for other tickets.

pr.body: Approach: tasktracker/dates.py adds InvalidDate(ValueError). parse_due validates calendar dates instead of clamping, raises InvalidDate for unsupported forms and for non-+Nd offsets, keeps today/tomorrow, case-insensitive matching and whitespace stripping. +0d is today; +Nd is N days after today; overflow raises InvalidDate. Key files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_dates.py (9 new tests). Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -> 13 tests, OK, exit 0 (baseline 4). Whole-change review agt_01M8GQMGMDQ8467CTPRY347PCD: pass, no blocking findings. Follow-ups (non-blocking, not changed): parse_due has one assert, house rule asks two (add str check on text); ISO/OFFSET regexes use \d which accepts non-ASCII digits (pre-existing; switch to [0-9]). Assumptions: behaviour change 2026-02-30 no longer clamps is intended per TT-101; the repo has no CHANGELOG file.
pr.summary: made parse_due reject impossible dates. now 2026-02-30 raises InvalidDate. before: clamped to 2026-02-28, now: InvalidDate with original text. unsupported forms and -Nd/Nd offsets raise InvalidDate.
pr.title: TT-101: reject impossible and malformed due dates

agt_01M8GQJQ9W7CQT0RDSB7KND3RB:1.description: parse_due has only one assert (`isinstance(today, date)`); the house rule asks for at least two meaningful assertions per non-trivial function. Follow-up: add an input-shape check on `text` (str) before `.strip()`. Asserts are also stripped under -O, so this is a follow-up, not a fix blocker.

agt_01M8GQJQ9W7CQT0RDSB7KND3RB:2.description: ISO and OFFSET regexes use `\d`, which matches non-ASCII Unicode digits; `int()` accepts them, so inputs like Arabic-Indic digits parse as dates. This predates the change. Follow-up: switch to `[0-9]` for strict ASCII matching.
